meta.description: Infers developmental trajectories, pseudotime, RNA velocity, and directed fate probabilities from single-cell data using PAGA, Slingshot, Monocle3, DPT, Palantir, scVelo, and CellRank 2. Use when ordering cells along a differentiation continuum, choosing a trajectory method by topology, rooting pseudotime, estimating RNA velocity direction, computing fate probabilities near a bifurcation, or judging whether an inferred trajectory is real.

scientific_integrity.detail: All references unchanged from the original audit's PASS finding; no fabricated statistics, DOIs, or results in any of the 9 executed outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Population-level computational biology methodology only; no individual diagnostic/prescriptive claims; out of clinical scope entirely.

methodological_ground.detail: Rigorous methodological framing preserved and further validated: new Input A independently confirmed the Governing Principle's root-sensitivity claim (rule 3) empirically on real data, rather than merely re-asserting it.

code_usability.detail: All 9 executed code-based inputs completed successfully with correct, real-data-validated results. Both original P1 code-usability defects (scVelo dynamical/stochastic crashes, CellRank fate-mapping crashes) are resolved: scVelo's compatibility note is independently verified accurate (including a deeper investigation into whether a call-site monkeypatch could recover dynamical mode -- it partially can, but the downstream latent_time() step re-triggers the same unfixable numpy internals bug, confirming the fixer's practical conclusion), and CellRank's fixed code runs with no RuntimeError/ValueError on real branching data.

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive real coverage of topology (PAGA), pseudotime (DPT), fate probabilities (Palantir, CellRank, now including VelocityKernel), R methods (Slingshot, tradeSeq) and RNA velocity (scVelo). The prior 1-point deduction for undocumented broken modes is resolved: the RNA Velocity section now accurately documents which mode works and why, independently verified correct.

reliability.note: The 'Version Compatibility' preamble continues to guide real recovery. Both original P1 recovery gaps are closed: scVelo has a documented, verified working fallback (deterministic + velocity_pseudotime), and CellRank has allow_overlap=True inline plus a Windows guard note. Docked 1 point: the CellRank guard is described in a comment rather than built into the code fence (see P2).

performance_context.note: SKILL.md grew from ~207 to ~242 lines to carry the new compatibility notes, still concise for a 7-method Complex skill relative to its real, now-accurate scope.

agent_usability.note: Governing Principle + Method Decision Table + Common Errors table remain exemplary; the Common Errors table now correctly covers all 4 real failure modes hit during the original audit (scVelo modes, CellRank Windows guard, PAGA threshold, tradeSeq raw counts) -- Inputs 3-6 all regression-tested clean this round. human_usability.note: Clear structure preserved; the mandatory redundancy pass removed genuine duplication from usage-guide.md (Tips section, restated Governing Principle content) without losing any unique information -- verified nothing deleted was unique to usage-guide.md.

security.note: No credentials, no unsafe eval/exec patterns, no destructive operations in any reviewed or executed code; unchanged from the original audit.

recommendations.title: CellRank code fence is not self-contained -- guard is a comment, not built in
recommendations.problem: The CellRank code block's Windows multiprocessing-guard requirement is documented in a comment above the fence ('Run this block inside if __name__ == "__main__":') but the fence itself is not wrapped, so a literal copy-paste into a standalone .py file still crashes with the original RuntimeError until the agent manually applies the guard.
recommendations.root_cause: A markdown code fence meant to be pasted inline into a larger script cannot itself contain the enclosing if __name__ guard without restructuring the whole example as a standalone script.
recommendations.fix: Either ship the CellRank example as a complete standalone script (like examples/scvelo_velocity.py) with the guard built in, or add one line making the requirement impossible to miss, e.g. a one-line minimal scaffold showing `if __name__ == "__main__": <indented block>`.

recommendations.title: CellRank's VelocityKernel path with deterministic-mode velocity is not caveated
recommendations.problem: This re-audit's new Input B found that feeding the fix's own recommended mode='deterministic' velocity into CellRank's VelocityKernel gives much weaker fate-probability entropy separation (0.36 vs 0.32) than the PseudotimeKernel route documented and tested elsewhere in the Skill (1.79 vs 0.82).
recommendations.root_cause: Deterministic mode is the Skill's own 'least recommended... quick first pass' option; its weaker per-cell velocity estimates propagate into weaker CellRank fate discrimination when used as a VelocityKernel input, but this specific combination is not called out.
recommendations.fix: Add a short note near the CellRank section or the RNA Velocity compatibility note: when only mode='deterministic' velocity is available, prefer PseudotimeKernel (or another non-velocity-derived direction source) over VelocityKernel for fate mapping, or explicitly flag that VelocityKernel fate probabilities inherit deterministic mode's weaker discrimination.

recommendations.title: monocle3_trajectory.R ships as an example but remains untested on this platform
recommendations.problem: Unchanged from the original audit: Monocle3/SeuratWrappers do not install on Windows in this environment (confirmed by TOOLS.md), so examples/monocle3_trajectory.R has never been executed by any audit.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill correctly frames Monocle3 as a documented alternative rather than the primary path (now that primary_tool is PAGA), but the shipped example itself carries no compatibility note of its own.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line note at the top of examples/monocle3_trajectory.R matching the Installation section's Windows caveat, so an agent reading the example file alone (without SKILL.md context) is not misled.
